name: Outdoor Concrete Lot
description: Open outdoor forecourt with a mid-grey concrete surface, a low green treeline across the horizon and soft overcast daylight.

lighting.type: Soft overcast daylight with broad even sky illumination
lighting.direction: Diffuse from above with no strong directional source

walls.material: Open horizon with a low deciduous treeline

shadow.style: Soft diffuse contact shadow with minimal directional cast

scene.reflection_environment: Broad overcast sky above, muted green treeline at the horizon and matte grey concrete below

reflections.permitted_pattern: Broad soft neutral sky reflections on upward-facing glass, roof and bonnet; a restrained muted green treeline band at the horizon line on upright glass and upper paint; subtle grey concrete fill on lower bodywork; diffuse low-contrast highlights with no hard specular edges
reflections.remove: Indoor fluorescent or LED strips, workshop walls and ceilings, source buildings, garage doors, signs, nearby vehicles, people and every other recognisable shape inherited from the source photograph
reflections.surface_guidance: On the side doors and rear-quarter paint, remove wavy bright patches and object-shaped source reflections. Replace them with a smooth vertical gradient of soft sky above and muted treeline at the horizon, following the panel curvature and continuing coherently across adjacent doors. Overcast light is even, so avoid inventing bright specular streaks. Preserve metallic paint, clear-coat gloss and panel contours; do not make the paint matte, flat, blurred or newly recoloured.
reflections.glass_guidance: On the windscreen and side glass, use soft neutral overcast sky in the upper portion easing into a restrained muted green treeline toward the horizon line. Avoid a flat blue wash, hard specular streaks and any indoor reflection pattern. Keep the glass transparent enough for realistic cabin visibility and preserve the windscreen frame, mirrors, dashboard and occupants if present.

scene.overall_look: Natural, evenly lit outdoor vehicle listing photograph

harmonisation.objective: Transform the completed composite into a natural single-exposure outdoor photograph under soft overcast daylight, replacing all source-environment reflections.
harmonisation.quality_target: Visually indistinguishable from an authentic vehicle listing photograph captured naturally on this forecourt in overcast daylight.

name: Outdoor Black Dealership Lot
description: Modern black industrial dealership building with roller doors, a clear blue sky and a large light-grey concrete forecourt in direct daylight.

lighting.type: Clear daylight with direct sun and open-sky fill

walls.material: Black metal cladding and dark roller doors

shadow.style: Medium-hard directional contact and cast shadow
shadow.direction: Slightly right and rear from the vehicle

scene.reflection_environment: Clear blue sky above, black dealership facade behind and light concrete below

reflections.permitted_pattern: Broad blue-sky reflections on upward-facing glass, roof and bonnet surfaces; restrained dark facade bands on upright paint and glass; subtle light-grey concrete fill on lower bodywork; small crisp daylight highlights from the upper left; no indoor ceiling or LED-panel reflections
reflections.remove: Indoor fluorescent or LED strips, workshop walls, source buildings, source signs, nearby vehicles, trees in implausible directions and every other recognisable shape inherited from the source photograph
reflections.surface_guidance: On the side doors and rear-quarter paint, remove wavy bright patches, green colour contamination and object-shaped source reflections. Replace them with restrained continuous dark-facade bands and subtle cool open-sky fill that follow the vehicle's panel curvature and continue coherently across adjacent doors. Preserve metallic paint, clear-coat gloss, panel contours and natural specular highlights; do not make the paint matte, flat, blurred, uniformly dark or newly recoloured.
reflections.glass_guidance: On the windscreen, use a natural non-uniform combination of clear blue-sky reflection and a restrained dark-facade influence toward the lower angle-facing glass. Avoid a flat cyan wash or generic studio reflection. Keep the glass transparent enough for realistic cabin visibility and preserve the windscreen frame, mirror, dashboard and occupants if present.

scene.overall_look: Clean, bright, naturally photographed outdoor dealership listing

harmonisation.objective: Transform the completed composite into a natural single-exposure outdoor dealership photograph while matching the clear-day lighting and replacing all source-environment reflections.
harmonisation.quality_target: Visually indistinguishable from an authentic vehicle listing photograph captured naturally on this outdoor dealership forecourt.

reflections.remove: Workshop walls, doors, signs, nearby vehicles and source-scene objects
reflections.surface_guidance: Preserve the physically plausible showroom reflections already established on the vehicle. Improve only the paint finish by adding natural clear-coat lustre, richer original paint-colour depth and slightly stronger specular contrast with smooth highlight falloff across curved panels. Do not remove, reposition, redraw or dim the existing overhead LED and recessed-spot reflections. Do not change the vehicle's paint colour, over-saturate it, flatten it, make it matte, or create artificial HDR, plastic or CGI shine.
